mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate relative to historical averages compresses equity discount rates, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors seek yield in equities.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 4.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate a broad-based contraction in consumer demand, triggering negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as recession risks rise.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict negative SPX 60-day returns in more than 60% of cases, with Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a manufacturing supply shock regime characterized by declining industrial production (INDPRO < 100), S&P 500 forward returns become negative over the next 20 trading days due to reduced corporate output and profit margins.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO falls below 100.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained expansion in real GDP (GDPC1 > 23000 billion) signals robust economic growth, supporting corporate earnings and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of quarters when GDPC1 exceeds 23000.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPI inflation rate above 3.5% signals persistent inflationary pressure, prompting central bank tightening and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months when CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.5%.

mechanism_narrative: In a labor market recovery regime with accelerating job growth (PAYEMS > 150,000 monthly additions), S&P 500 forward returns become positive over the next 5 trading days due to rising consumer spending and corporate investment.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS exceeds 150,000.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in the federal funds rate and CPI inflation (FEDFUNDS > 5.0% and CPIAUCSL > 3.5%) signal aggressive monetary tightening amid high inflation, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as real rates rise and growth fears intensify.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL fails to predict negative SPX 60-day returns in more than 60% of cases, with Rank IC < 0.03.
